BAKDI Malika, Professor at university of khemis miliana

Absteact: 
This study explores the role of corporate governance in attracting Foreign Direct 
Investment (FDI) in Algeria through an analytical approach. Corporate governance, 
which ensures transparency, accountability, and protection of investors’ rights, has 
become a central determinant for international investors when selecting host countries. 
Algeria, despite its strategic geographical location and abundant natural resources, has 
struggled to secure sustainable inflows of FDI compared to other emerging economies. 
The paper examines how governance mechanisms, such as regulatory frameworks, 
shareholder protection, board structures, and disclosure practices; affect investor 
confidence and decision-making. It also highlights the institutional challenges in 
Algeria, including bureaucratic inefficiencies, weak enforcement of corporate laws, 
and limited financial market development, which constrain its attractiveness to foreign 
investors. Using an analytical framework, the study evaluates the extent to which 
improving governance standards could strengthen Algeria’s investment climate, 
diversify its economy, and enhance long-term competitiveness. The findings suggest 
that strengthening corporate governance practices is essential for Algeria to reduce 
investment risks, improve transparency, and integrate more effectively into the global 
economy. 
Key words: corporate goverance, investors, FDI.

Abstract 
This paper examines the role of accounting disclosure in strengthening the effective 
implementation of corporate governance in Algeria. It argues that transparent and 
reliable disclosure is not only a technical process but also a foundation for ethical and 
accountable management. Using a descriptive and analytical approach, the study 
explores the theoretical relationship between disclosure and governance, analyzes 
current practices in developing countries, and identifies major barriers within the 
Algerian context. The findings highlight that weak enforcement, limited professional 
training, and cultural resistance to transparency remain the main challenges. The 
paper proposes regulatory, institutional, and managerial mechanisms to enhance the 
disclosure–governance relationship and strengthen the credibility of the accounting 
and auditing profession. Ultimately, it concludes that improving disclosure quality is 
essential for building trust, accountability, and sustainable corporate governance in 
Algeria.

Absteact: 
This study explores the role of corporate governance in attracting Foreign Direct 
Investment (FDI) in Algeria through an analytical approach. Corporate governance, 
which ensures transparency, accountability, and protection of investors’ rights, has 
become a central determinant for international investors when selecting host countries. 
Algeria, despite its strategic geographical location and abundant natural resources, has 
struggled to secure sustainable inflows of FDI compared to other emerging economies. 
The paper examines how governance mechanisms, such as regulatory frameworks, 
shareholder protection, board structures, and disclosure practices; affect investor 
confidence and decision-making. It also highlights the institutional challenges in 
Algeria, including bureaucratic inefficiencies, weak enforcement of corporate laws, 
and limited financial market development, which constrain its attractiveness to foreign 
investors. Using an analytical framework, the study evaluates the extent to which 
improving governance standards could strengthen Algeria’s investment climate, 
diversify its economy, and enhance long-term competitiveness. The findings suggest 
that strengthening corporate governance practices is essential for Algeria to reduce 
investment risks, improve transparency, and integrate more effectively into the global 
economy.

Abstract 
This paper examines the role of accounting disclosure in strengthening the effective 
implementation of corporate governance in Algeria. It argues that transparent and 
reliable disclosure is not only a technical process but also a foundation for ethical and 
accountable management. Using a descriptive and analytical approach, the study 
explores the theoretical relationship between disclosure and governance, analyzes 
current practices in developing countries, and identifies major barriers within the 
Algerian context. The findings highlight that weak enforcement, limited professional 
training, and cultural resistance to transparency remain the main challenges. The 
paper proposes regulatory, institutional, and managerial mechanisms to enhance the 
disclosure–governance relationship and strengthen the credibility of the accounting 
and auditing profession. Ultimately, it concludes that improving disclosure quality is 
essential for building trust, accountability, and sustainable corporate governance in 
Algeria.

Abstract : 
 
Our study aims to examine the determinants and incentives of accounting disclosure for 
companies within developing countries, particularly Algeria. Because it has a significant impact on 
the quality of financial information, especially in international accounting harmonization era.  
We found that both the ownership concentration and tax compliance are the two main 
incentives that significantly affect the quality of accounting disclosure for Algerian companies.  
Moreover, in second place, the financial market activity volume and loans.
